answer.why_different: The generated document appears to have substituted the specification's abstract notification target variable for the callback runtime expression, and then emitted both a non-runtime key and an incorrectly formatted runtime-expression key. This is an address/structure difference: the callback target is declared under different keys, with the required notificationRecipientAddress expression omitted and two alternative entries added.
answer.spec_3gpp: The notification POST is mapped to the resource URI {notificationTarget}, whose value is the notificationRecipientAddress contained in the subscription. The notifyMOIChanges request body is NotifyMoiChanges, and the response is 204 on success or 4xx/5xx with ErrorResponse.
answer.openapi: A Callback Object key must be a runtime expression enclosed in braces, such as {$request.body#/url}. Runtime expressions use the $request.body form and may reference a request-body property; {notificationTarget} is not such an expression, while $request.body#/notificationTarget without surrounding braces is not a valid callback key.
answer.clearer_why: The official side has one callback entry with a valid runtime-expression key that directly identifies the notification recipient address. The generated side has two duplicate-looking entries, uses an invalid callback key form, and does not clearly identify the correct source property.

citations.quote: notificationTarget   URI of the notification target on the MnS consumer, contained in the notification subscription, see notificationRecipientAddress defined in clause 4.3.22.2 in TS 28.622 [11].
{expression} | [Path Item Object](#path-item-object) | A Path Item Object used to define a callback request and expected responses.

differences.reason: The generated side omits the callback keyed by the notificationRecipientAddress runtime expression, losing the official callback target association. The official context contains "'{request.body#/notificationRecipientAddress}':" (C1), and the specification identifies notificationRecipientAddress as the source of notificationTarget (S11).

The added key `{notificationTarget}` uses the specification's abstract resource-URI variable as if it were an OpenAPI callback expression. OpenAPI requires a callback key in the `{expression}` form (O4), and the specification distinguishes notificationTarget from the subscription's notificationRecipientAddress (S11).

The added key `$request.body#/notificationTarget` is not enclosed in the braces required for a Callback Object patterned key (O4), and it references notificationTarget rather than the notificationRecipientAddress property identified by the specification (S11).

#### Callback Object  
A map of possible out-of band callbacks related to the parent operation.
Each value in the map is a [Path Item Object](#path-item-object) that describes a set of requests that may be initiated by the API provider and the expected responses.
The key value used to identify the callback object is an expression, evaluated at runtime, that identifies a URL to use for the callback operation.  
##### Patterned Fields
Field Pattern | Type | Description
---|:---:|---

Note that in the use of `operationRef`, the _escaped forward-slash_ is necessary when
using JSON references.  
##### Runtime Expressions  
Runtime expressions allow defining values based on information that will only be available within the HTTP message in an actual API call.
This mechanism is used by [Link Objects](#link-object) and [Callback Objects](#callback-object).  
The runtime expression is defined by the following [ABNF](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc5234) syntax  
```
expression = ( "$url" | "$method" | "$statusCode" | "$request." source | "$response." source )
source = ( header-reference | query-reference | path-reference | body-reference )
header-reference = "header." token
query-reference = "query." name
path-reference = "path." name

evidence.query: callback runtime expression URL of the notification request body {request.body#/notificationRecipientAddress} {notificationTarget} $request.body#/notificationTarget
evidence.title: Examples

source = ( header-reference | query-reference | path-reference | body-reference )
header-reference = "header." token
query-reference = "query." name
path-reference = "path." name
body-reference = "body" ["#" fragment]
fragment = a JSON Pointer [RFC 6901](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6901)
name = *( char )
char = as per RFC [7159](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7159#section-7)
token = as per RFC [7230](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7230#section-3.2.6)
```  
The `name` identifier is case-sensitive, whereas `token` is not.
